clue.text: Collection of tiny moving parts in old-fashioned timer

definitions.text: Collection of tiny moving parts in old-fashioned timer

blocks.clueFragment: Collection of tiny moving parts in old-fashioned timer
blocks.note: surface reading: a clockmaker's box of cogs, springs, gears from an antique clock
setter's reading: the moving parts are grains trickling through an hourglass

explanation.surface: A tray of minute gears and springs taken from an antique clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving parts' suggests clockwork, but the old-fashioned timer is an hourglass, whose working parts are countless grains.
explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass measures time by fine grains falling from one bulb to the other, so its moving parts are a heap of grains.

clue.text: Crazy bloke I accost, dropping charge

definitions.note: maniac is mostly a noun but is also used as an adjective, as in 'maniac driving'

indicators.note: dropping means letting something fall away, so the word for charge is removed from the word before it

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
taken as written
taken as written
a charge is a cost or price

explanation.surface: A man stops someone in the street but asks no fee; it sounds deranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like an accusation, but it means a price, which is taken off the end of the word before.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniac is a wildly mad person, and the word can describe frenzied, unhinged behaviour.

clue.text: Pack coming from bridge player to opponent

blocks.note: the four bridge players are North, South, East and West; South is S
taken as written
West sits beside South at bridge and is an opponent

explanation.surface: A deck of cards being passed from one bridge player to the player opposing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like a pack of cards, fitting the bridge picture, but it is the verb meaning to stash away.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow something is to pack it away neatly in a space, as luggage is stowed.

clue.text: Initially play a part in conditional release

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: first letter of play
taken as written
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An actor on licence from prison takes a small stage part as one of the release conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is the early release of a prisoner on condition of good behaviour, a conditional release.

clue.text: Gains, we hear, inspired teachers

indicators.note: we hear says the word for gains is to be judged by its sound when spoken

blocks.note: gains are profits, which is said the same way

explanation.surface: Reports say that some gifted teachers have made money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' reads as 'gifted', but here it means divinely inspired, as prophets are.
explanation.definitionFit: Prophets are religious teachers believed to speak by divine inspiration.

clue.text: Kind of lender that's manipulated person with less money

blocks.note: a pawn is someone used and manipulated by others
broker read as more broke, that is, having less money

explanation.surface: A moneylender who exploits someone already short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: BROKER is read as the comparative of broke, slang for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker lends money against goods left as security, so it is one sort of lender.

clue.text: Cause of visual problem producing fall

blocks.note: first meaning: clouding of the eye's lens
second meaning: a large, steep waterfall

explanation.surface: Something that blurs your sight and makes you trip over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' suggests a stumble caused by poor sight, but it is a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an opaque clouding of the eye's lens and a great cascade of water.

clue.text: In office of rival paper, occasionally

blocks.note: in and at both indicate location
The Times is a rival newspaper to the Sunday Telegraph's stable

explanation.surface: A journalist is now working at a competing newspaper's office.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter writes for the Telegraph, so the rival paper is The Times; being at its office is 'at Times'.
explanation.definitionFit: At times is an idiom for now and then, or occasionally.

clue.text: A woman from New York in Paris, say

blocks.note: taken as written
broad is American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: An American woman from New York visiting Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From New York' marks the slang as American; the definition is an example, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in Paris is one instance of being overseas, in a foreign country.

clue.text: Left to one's own resources in commercial break

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: Viewers left to amuse themselves while the TV programme pauses for adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adrift is without guidance or support, left to fend for themselves.

clue.text: Massive part of our capital, in statement

indicators.note: a statement is something spoken, so the place is to be identified by its sound

blocks.note: Wapping is a district of East London by the Thames

explanation.surface: Someone declares a big chunk of London to be enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: Wapping, in London's East End, sounds like the slangy adjective for huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Whopping is informal for very large or enormous.

clue.text: Crooked merchant confused backer with mere talk

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters that follow are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shady dealer bewildered his financial supporter with empty chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A black marketeer trades illegally in scarce or controlled goods, a dishonest kind of merchant.

clue.text: Loss an heir mishandled – that means less for everyone else

definitions.text: that means less for everyone else

indicators.note: something mishandled is botched and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An inheritance squandered, leaving the rest of the family short.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: what one party takes, others lose.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion's share is the largest portion, taken by one so that the remaining people get little.

clue.text: Dance in Scotland including very lively celebration

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the reel is a lively Scottish country dance
v is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A Highland dance as part of a very spirited party.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a noisy, merry celebration or festivity.

clue.text: Perform as striker returning for game

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: to flog is to strike or beat, acting as a striker

explanation.surface: Playing as a centre forward back in the side for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer, but here it is simply one who strikes, that is, whips.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played with clubs on a course, so it is a game.

clue.text: Female artist presented with gift, like perfume

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
a grant is a gift of money

explanation.surface: A woman painter receives a present that smells lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant means sweet-smelling, which describes a perfume.

clue.text: This is odd – without leader, it's the opposite

definitions.text: This is odd – without leader, it's the opposite

blocks.clueFragment: This is odd – without leader, it's the opposite
blocks.note: surface reading: a strange organisation whose leaderless members behave contrarily
setter's reading: the answer is an odd number, and its first letter removed leaves the word for its opposite

explanation.surface: Something strange that, once its head is gone, turns into its reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' reads as strange but means not divisible by two; drop the leading S and the word left is even, the opposite of odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is an odd number, and its last four letters spell the word for numbers that are not odd.

clue.text: Kind of pasta that's new, lots and lots

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
oodles means a great quantity

explanation.surface: A fresh pasta dish served in huge quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are long thin strips of dough, a form of pasta.

clue.text: It sounds like search for religious type

indicators.note: sounds like tells the solver to judge the next word by how it is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: to search is to seek

explanation.surface: Someone appears to be hunting for a devout person.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sikh is a follower of Sikhism, a religion founded in the Punjab.

clue.text: Sources of rumours corrupt Congressman is holding boy back

indicators.note: corrupt means debased or spoiled, so the politician's letters are scrambled
back tells the solver to read the word for boy from right to left
holding means grasping something within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Gossips spread a tale that a crooked American legislator is restraining a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled Congressman becomes SCANMONGERS, and the backwards boy goes in after SCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandalmongers spread malicious gossip, so they are where rumours start.

clue.text: Person using pencil found in part of desk

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who draws
second meaning: a sliding compartment in furniture

explanation.surface: An artist with a pencil turns up inside a desk compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both one who sketches and a sliding box fitted into a desk or chest.

clue.text: Threaten to go out, say, after midnight?

indicators.note: mid points to the centre of the word, so just its central letter is kept

blocks.note: the middle letter of night
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: Someone talking about leaving the house late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Midnight is read as the middle of night, its central letter; 'after' places UTTER behind it. A candle that gutters flickers as if about to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttering flame flickers and burns low, close to being extinguished.

clue.text: Quick to contain damage where drugs are sold

indicators.note: to contain means to hold something inside, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: pacy means fast or quick
harm is damage

explanation.surface: Hurry to limit the harm done, at the chemist's.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a shop dispensing medicines, a chemist's.

clue.text: Passage heading north on large sailboat

indicators.note: in a down entry heading north means travelling upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a passage is a way through
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A voyage northwards aboard a big sailing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing boat with a small mizzen mast set aft.

clue.text: E.g. a landlord?

blocks.note: first meaning: a is one character of the alphabet
second meaning: someone who lets property

explanation.surface: Is a landlord one example, the question asks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like the article, but it is the alphabet's first character, an instance of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a character of the alphabet and, read as let-ter, a person who rents out property.

clue.text: Issue great healer proverbially raised

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, and in a down entry that reads the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: the proverb says time is a great healer

explanation.surface: A doctor's famous cure-all is put forward as the topic for discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to issue or send out, as light or sound.

clue.text: Royal son ultimately put in charge?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is used
put in means placed inside, so the single letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: a charge is a price
last letter of son

explanation.surface: A king's son finally gets made responsible, with a question over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal son' reads like the definition, and indeed a prince is one, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a member of a royal family, so 'royal' works as a noun for him.

clue.text: Flower I water is ruined

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked and broken up, so the letters are reassembled in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener admits that watering has spoilt a plant in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing plant with hanging clusters of purple or white blossoms.
